extracted.intended_audience: new Wattpad authors / creators writing their first Wattpad story
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, platform-specific guidance for planning, drafting, and publishing a debut story on Wattpad aimed at building readership. Focuses on idea generation, structure, workflow, and community engagement for serial/web fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flesh out your ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Set a timer for 15 minutes and get all ideas on paper without editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freewrite rapidly to capture plot fragments, scenes, characters and beats; don't self-edit during this brainstorming session so you can surface unexpected directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an inspiring title
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick a title that keeps you focused and makes the project feel real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a working title that motivates you and frames the story while drafting; the title can change later but helps maintain momentum and clarity of purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write your synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a brief high-level summary of plot points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft a short synopsis to clarify main beats and trajectory; use it as a roadmap for pacing and to ensure cohesion across chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set writing goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Break the project into manageable tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define achievable targets (daily/weekly word counts, chapter milestones) to maintain steady progress rather than attempting to complete the whole story at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start small — and not at the beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with scenes or parts of the story rather than forcing Chapter 1 immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that a strong beginning often emerges after you finish the story; write compelling scenes you feel excited about and assemble the beginning later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow the story to evolve; modify subplots and characters as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect changes in direction as you discover your characters and plot; revising arcs and roles during drafting is normal and beneficial to the story's development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't edit while you write
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid revising as you draft; save revisions for after completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate drafting from editing to preserve creative momentum; resist polishing early drafts so you can finish and then return with fresh perspective for edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn how to build a captivated audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt strategies to grow readership: update frequently, edit properly, use appropriate chapter length and tags, and engage with the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical pointers include publishing regular updates, ensuring chapters are well-edited, aiming for chapters of ~1,500–2,000 words, using accurate and discoverable tags, and interacting with readers and other creators to build engagement.
